concerns.text: T003 is tagged [P] and scheduled in parallel with T002, but both tasks implement code in the SAME file (`code/data_loader.py`). Concurrent edits to one module with shared imports/config constitute hidden shared state; the [P] tag is unsafe. Either split into separate modules, serialize T002→T003, or scope each task to distinct functions with an explicit merge note.

T005 verifies `run_pipeline.sh --stage data --year 2019` and T011 runs `./run_pipeline.sh`, but no task CREATES `run_pipeline.sh`. T001 only documents it in quickstart.md ('Document the runnable entry point'). A consumer exists without a producer task; add creation of the script (with its stage subcommands) to T001 or a dedicated task before T005.

T003 uses `REGIONAL_SUBSET` and `MAX_GAP_DAYS` from `code/config.py` (T001) but declares no `[Depends on: T001]`. The stated execution order puts T001 first, so this is only a missing explicit edge; add the dependency tag for consistency with T004/T005 style.
